cards.text: Jesus has been born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod. Then visitors show up in Jerusalem: Magi from the east. No heads-up, no group text, they just ARRIVE.

cards.question: The Magi go around Jerusalem asking where to find someone who's just been born. What title do they give Him?
The Magi say they know about this newborn King because they saw His ___ in the east.
The Magi say they've come all this way to worship the newborn King.

cards.text: Word reaches King Herod. Picture it: strangers in HIS city asking where the King of the Jews is, like somebody in your office lobby asking, 'Which desk belongs to the NEW boss?'

cards.question: When King Herod hears the Magi's question, he is ___.
King Herod is the only one in Jerusalem who is disturbed by the news.

cards.text: Herod gathers all the chief priests and scribes of the people. He's got ONE question for them, and I bet you could hear a chocolate chip drop.

cards.question: What does Herod ask the chief priests and scribes?

answers.text: Where the Christ was to be born
When the Christ would finally come

cards.question: The chief priests and scribes tell Herod the Christ will be born in Bethlehem in Judea, and they're sure because an angel told them.

cards.text: The prophet's words speak right to the little town: Bethlehem is 'by no means least among the rulers of Judah.' Little Bethlehem just got moved to the TOP of the guest list.

cards.question: The prophecy says a ruler will come out of Bethlehem. What will He be to God's people Israel?

cards.text: Then Herod calls the Magi in secretly. You know that feeling when the boss says, 'Got a minute?' and then CLOSES THE DOOR?

cards.question: In that secret meeting, Herod learns from the Magi the exact ___ the star had appeared.

cards.text: Then Herod sends the Magi off to Bethlehem: 'Go and search carefully for the Child.' Search carefully. That's me every morning hunting for my timer under a pile of parchment paper.

cards.question: Herod tells the Magi to come back and report to him once they find the Child.
What reason does Herod give the Magi for wanting that report?

answers.text: So he can go and worship Him too
So he can send the Child a gift
So he can add Him to the records

cards.text: After hearing the king, the Magi head out, and the star they saw in the east goes ahead of them. No map app, no 'recalculating,' just a star leading the WAY.

cards.question: The star goes ahead of the Magi until it stops. Where does it stand?

answers.text: Over the place where the Child was

cards.question: When the Magi see the star, they ___.

cards.text: They come to the house and see the Child with His mother Mary. End of the road, friend. There He is.

cards.question: When the Magi see the Child, they fall down and worship Him.
After worshiping the Child, what do the Magi do next?

answers.text: Open their treasures and give gifts
Ask Mary to tell them about His birth
Sing a song of praise over Him

cards.text: Gold, frankincense and myrrh. Friend, the fanciest gift I ever gave was a cookie with EXTRA mango bits, and I walked around for a week thinking I'd outdone myself.
Then the Magi get a warning, and it comes in a dream.

cards.question: The Magi are warned in a dream not to do something. What is it?
After the dream, the Magi head home to their country by the same road they came.

cards.text: Hold onto your apron, friend. The next batch of this story is already in the oven.

findings.problem: No earlier card mentions or sets up a star, so the baker can only guess among star, angel and cloud. The blank tests an unseen word rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card retells the Magi asking where the King of the Jews is, which comes from Matthew 2:2, as well as Herod hearing the news in 2:3. Citing only Matthew 2:3 is too narrow; the card uses Matthew 2:2-3.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Identifying these as the prophet's words uses Matthew 2:5, while the quoted prophecy comes from 2:6. The citation of only Matthew 2:6 is too narrow; the card uses Matthew 2:5-6.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "In that secret meeting" points back to the setup on card 13, which is no longer on screen. The question should supply the context itself, such as by saying that Herod is meeting secretly with the Magi.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: Herod sending the Magi, "Search carefully.", and the timer joke. Non-opening story cards are limited to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "That report" points back to card 16 without explaining the report in this question. The question should say that Herod wants the Magi to report to him after they find the Child.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the Magi arriving and seeing the Child, "End of the road, friend.", and "There He is." It needs to be reduced to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
